# What drives ecological stability?

<p class="hero-name">Samuel R.P-J. Ross</p>

::: {.intro-grid}

::: {.intro-lead}
I study why some ecosystems remain stable or can rapidly recover from environmental change, while others collapse.
:::

::: {.intro-text}
I'm an Associate Professor in the Hakubi Center for Advanced Research and Graduate School of Agriculture at Kyoto University in Japan. My research combines ecological concepts and methods with high-resolution data to understand the mechanisms underpinning ecological stability.

<span class="jp-label">生態系の安定性・レジリエンス・応答多様性・生態音響学</span>
:::

:::

::: {.research-card .research-rd}

<div class="research-number">01</div>
<div class="research-label">RESPONSE DIVERSITY</div>

<h3>Exploring concepts and methods for predicting stability</h3>

<p>Understanding biological insurance mechanisms, such as how differences among organisms' responses to environmental change can generate stability.</p>

<a href="research.qmd#response-diversity">Find out more <span>→</span></a>

:::
 

::: {.research-card .research-acoustic}

<div class="research-number">02</div>
<div class="research-label">ECOACOUSTICS</div>

<h3>Ecological big data for measuring real-world stability and change</h3>

<p>Using passive acoustic monitoring of natural soundscapes to observe ecosystem dynamics across spatial and temporal scales relevant to ecosystem management.</p>

<a href="research.qmd#ecoacoustics">Find out more <span>→</span></a>
